  "text": "The stone was smaller than she expected. Elias stood beside it while she worked one shoe loose, holding the heel with both hands.

“Don’t empty it there,” he said.

She looked up.

“Ants.”

A thin procession crossed the dry earth between his boots. She tipped the muddy water toward the river instead.

For a while this occupied them: the other shoe, the stockings, a place to put them where they would not slide away.

“Have you seen Father?” she asked.

“No.”

“He died in winter.”

Elias moved his foot to let the ants pass.

“Was it a hard one?”

“The winter?”

He nodded.

“Yes.”

Across the water, something knocked against the boat. The ferryman lifted his pole, examined its end, and lowered it again.

“I stayed with him,” Mara said. “At the end.”

“All right.”

“I thought you ought to know.”

“All right.”

She rubbed a thumb over the seam of her stocking. There was a hole she had meant to mend before leaving.

“He called me by your name.”

Elias bent his knees and sat on the ground. He did it awkwardly, with one hand braced behind him, and she remembered that he had always been awkward about sitting, even as a boy.

“Did you answer?”

“Yes.”

He picked up a twig and laid it across the ants’ path. They divided around it. He watched, then took it away.

“What did he want?”

“Water. The lamp moved.”

“Was that all?”

“That was all.”

Mara folded the stocking over her knee.

“I moved it,” she said.

Elias nodded, and this time she believed he had heard her."
